name: projectm
why: A Milkdrop-compatible visualizer that turns music into evolving generative imagery, a classic audio-to-visual transform.

brief.what_it_is: projectM is an open-source music visualizer that reimplements Winamp's Milkdrop visualizer as a cross-platform library, libprojectM. It takes in audio PCM data and produces OpenGL-rendered visuals driven by Milkdrop-style preset files, which combine pixel shaders and equations. The README says the library analyzes audio with beat detection and FFT, then applies the active preset to those audio features. This repository holds only the library, not an end-user app. The frontends are separate repositories, and the README names projectMSDL as the canonical one.
brief.why_it_exists: The README describes projectM as a modern, cross-platform, reusable reimplementation of the Milkdrop visualizer by Geiss, whose purpose is to read audio input and produce mesmerizing visuals by rendering advanced equations into a limitless array of user-contributed visualizations.
brief.how_it_works: Preset files define each visualization through pixel shaders and Milkdrop-style equations and parameters, and the library ships without presets. libprojectM parses presets, analyzes PCM audio with beat detection and FFT, applies the preset to the audio feature data, and renders the result with OpenGL either to a dedicated context or to a texture.
brief.install_notes: The README gives no install commands. It points to docs/building.rst for building libprojectM from source with CMake, to docs/emscripten.rst for WebAssembly builds, and to the project wiki for developer documentation. The library depends mainly on OpenGL. End-user visuals need a frontend such as projectMSDL, which uses libSDL2 for audio input, and a preset pack. The base Milkdrop texture pack is recommended for use with any preset pack. The README says the projectM library does not ship with presets. Its Homebrew formula is the old 3.1.12 release, per the README.
brief.standout: The project is a clean split between a reusable C/C++ rendering library and separate frontends, with the Milkdrop preset format as the shared language. Presets are community-made and kept out of the library, and the README lists packs of roughly 10K, 4K, and 130K+ presets, with a 4.08GB MegaPack.
brief.status: Appears maintained. Five build-status badges (Windows, Linux, macOS, Emscripten, Android) point to GitHub Actions workflows on master, and the README calls the project under heavy development. I did not find a release date or last-commit date in the fetched page, so I cannot confirm recency beyond that.
brief.caveats: The README says the end-user frontends are development previews that are not feature-complete and may have bugs. The Homebrew and Steam listings are for the old 3.1.12 release, and the README says the Homebrew formula is the old 3.1.12 release. Frontends and presets live in other repositories, so this repo alone will not show visuals. Licence is LGPL-2.1 for the core library. The README warns that up- and downstream projects may use different licences. The Android apps and ProjectM TV are third-party and not supported by the developers. The MegaPack is 4.08GB zipped. The scout note's executables (projectM-unittest, projectMSDL) are not mentioned in the README, which describes projectMSDL as a separate repository.
quotes: Experience psychedelic and mesmerizing visuals by transforming music into equations that render into a limitless array of user-contributed visualizations.
This repository now only contains the projectM shared/static library. All frontends, plug-ins and other tools were outsourced into separate repositories.
The projectM library does not ship with any presets.

links.label: Cream of the Crop preset pack (about 10K presets)

judge.reason: Milkdrop presets turn live audio features into shader-driven generative imagery, an unusually tangible audio-to-visual transform; the separate frontend makes setup less immediate but not fatal.

entry.title: projectM
entry.tldr: An open-source reimplementation of Winamp's Milkdrop visualizer that turns live audio into evolving OpenGL imagery driven by community-made preset files.
entry.deeper_look:
projectM is a library, libprojectM, that takes in raw audio samples and renders visuals with OpenGL. It runs beat detection and an FFT over the audio, then feeds those features into a preset. Each preset is a Milkdrop-style file made of pixel shaders plus equations and parameters, so a whole visualization is a small piece of math that reacts to sound.

It exists as a modern, cross-platform, reusable take on Milkdrop, the Winamp visualizer written by Geiss. The README puts the goal this way: "Experience psychedelic and mesmerizing visuals by transforming music into equations that render into a limitless array of user-contributed visualizations."

The interesting design choice is the split. The repository holds only the rendering library. Frontends, plug-ins and tools live in separate repositories, and the Milkdrop preset format is the shared language between them. The README names projectMSDL as the canonical frontend, and it uses SDL2 to capture audio input. The library ships with no presets at all. Community packs fill that gap, ranging from about 4K and 10K presets up to a 130K+ MegaPack that weighs 4.08GB zipped.

That makes it a door into generative graphics. Presets are readable equations and shaders, so you can open one, change a number, and watch what the music does to it.
entry.install:
brew install projectm
# Presets are not included. Download a pack separately, e.g. the Cream of the Crop pack (about 10K presets) from the projectM GitHub organisation, plus the base Milkdrop texture pack.
# Needs an audio source for the visuals to react to.

try_this.what_happens: Lists the options of the SDL frontend, which is the way to see visuals from this install.

entry.whats_unique: It keeps the Milkdrop preset format alive outside Winamp, so decades of community-made visualizations still run, on a library other programs can embed.
entry.caveats: The Homebrew formula is the old 3.1.12 release, the README calls the frontends development previews that are not feature-complete, and no presets come with it.
